dimensions.assessment: Affects federal land management agencies, landowners along the trail route, volunteer/nonprofit organizations, and trail users.
dimensions.evidence: consult with other Federal agencies, affected State, Tribal, and local governments, landowners... and other interested parties

dimensions.assessment: Directs administrative prioritization, planning, and coordination to finish a continuous trail route without granting new eminent domain authority.
dimensions.evidence: Nothing in this Act--provides any authority to acquire land or interests in land for inclusion in the Trail beyond the authorities provided... including acquisition by eminent domain

dimensions.assessment: Subject to appropriations, requires anticipated cost estimates in the development plan, but does not set a specific funding amount.
dimensions.evidence: Subject to the availability of appropriations... including anticipated costs of the plans

dimensions.assessment: Directs specific executive actions for one designated national scenic trail, including a joint completion team and a comprehensive development plan.
dimensions.evidence: require the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Interior to prioritize the completion of the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail

dimensions.assessment: Sets a 10-year timeline for trail completion and requires a comprehensive development plan within 3 years.
dimensions.evidence: complete the Trail as a continuous route not later than 10 years after the date of enactment of this Act

missing_information: Total cost to complete the trail
Exact miles of uncompleted trail gaps remaining
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the USDA and Department of the Interior to prioritize and seek to complete the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail within 10 years, establish a joint completion team, create a comprehensive development plan, and partner with nonprofits.
